programmes.d: After exposing Kane's plan to reduce the population of the Ark, Abby and Chancellor Jaha notice a signal from Earth and realize at least some of the 100 must still be alive.
While Bellamy leads his crew into Grounder territory in a search for Olivia, Raven can't help but notice the deep connection between Finn and Clarke.
An unfamiliar case is familiar to Peter.
Lincoln works a case "over there" with the Alt Fringe team.
Walter travels to the Alternate Universe to help Broyles.
In this mind-bending episode, the story jumps ahead to 2036 when the Fringe team strikes back against the Observers in a game-changing battle.
The Cortexiphan children surface with new developments.
A case of spontaneous combustion forces Walter to revisit his painful past, while the Fringe team faces off against David Robert Jones to save the world — or worlds.
In the Season Four finale, the Fringe team is pushed to their breaking point as they desperately attempt to prevent a catastrophic event threatening the lives of everyone.
In the fifth and final season premiere, Peter and his daughter Etta (GEORGINA HAIG) set out to find out what happened to Olivia.
While Clarke and Raven make contact with the Ark, Abby is removed from the council and Jaha reveals that there are not enough drop ships for everyone on the Ark.
While some of the 100 accidentally eat hallucinogenic nuts, Clarke and Bellamy go on a mission to find supplies for winter and are brought closer by a terrifying event.
All hell breaks loose when Clarke and Finn attempt to broker peace with the Grounders. And tragedy strikes during the Unity Day celebration on the Ark.
Murphy returns to camp claiming to have been held captive and tortured by the Grounders, and Clarke and Bellamy have very different opinions on how to handle his return.
With a low food supply at camp, Clarke and Finn lead a group out to hunt for food and wind up with Finn's life in danger. Meanwhile, Raven makes Bellamy an offer he can't refuse.
Should they stay or should they go: Those remaining on the Ark must come to terms with the inevitable. Meanwhile, Clarke and Finn find themselves facing a new enemy.
It's the end of the world as we know it in the first season finale as the conflict on the ground comes to a head and the situation on the Ark comes to a stunning conclusion.
In the season premiere, Clarke is still trapped, while the fate of Bellamy, Finn & Raven is still unknown. Meanwhile, the survivors of the Ark face a dangerous new world.
The Fringe team revisits Walter's Harvard lab — now under Observer control — to locate information they need to fight on in their mission to save the world.
As the Fringe team continues to fight the Observers, unforeseen events lead them into a forest, where they encounter a strange subculture devoted to recording human history.
When the Fringe Team tracks a lead into a hostile and heavily guarded location, Phillip Broyles (series star LANCE REDDICK) resurfaces… but can he be trusted?
The Fringe Team goes on the offensive.
A key piece needed to defeat the Observers is uncovered.
The Fringe Team orchestrates a Fringe event of their own.
Clarke demands answers from President Wallace. Kane interrogates one of The 100, and Abby performs emergency surgery. Meanwhile, Octavia resorts to violence to find Lincoln.
Nothing is what it seems. When Clarke (ELIZA TAYLOR) discovers a horrifying project being carried out in Mount Weather's medical ward, she joins forces with an unlikely ally.
After being betrayed, Clarke takes matters into her own hands and proves she's not going down without a flight. Bellamy, Finn and Murphy race against time to save a stranger.
While Kane (HENRY IAN CUSICK) leads a mission to make peace with the Grounders, Lincoln (RICKY WHITTLE) enters a world of pain. And Finn's search for Clarke takes a violent turn.
Tensions run high between Clarke & Finn, while Octavia faces her worst nightmare. As Jasper & Monty discover the truth about Mt. Weather, Wallace is about to be betrayed.
